subject: Creating a User Defined Distribution: sampling

messages.author: bb78530a53062d83
messages.subject: Creating a User Defined Distribution: sampling
parts:
Hello everyone!

I am working on a project where I would like to define my own distribution and use MCMC through NIMBLE. I heard NIMBLE allowed one to create user defined distributions, as long as I had the pdf and a way to sample from it. However, when I read through the manual on the topic, the example given gave the exponential distribution, which has a nice closed form solution if one wants to use inverse transform sampling. The distribution I want to use (which models the behavior of the p-value in a one sample z-test) probably does not have a closed form inverse cdf, since part of the distribution involves the quantile function of the normal distribution. Are there examples out there of users using other methods (such as accept reject sampling) or using a non-closed form representation of the inverse cdf of a user defined distribution in order to do MCMC in NIMBLE? 

Thanks a million! Good luck out there with all the virus stuff. Hope ya'll are staying safe and healthy.

messages.author: 5fa2a363d4ddd1d1
messages.subject: Re: Creating a User Defined Distribution: sampling
parts:
hi Matt,

If the algorithm you'll be using doesn't simulate from the distributions (this is true of NIMBLE's built-in MCMC samplers) then you only need to define the density ('d') function and not the random generation ('r') function. Our documentation on this point has been a bit inconsistent/confusing -- we're trying to clean things up on that front (and please email me separately if you have noticed any confusing documentation that led to your email). So you may not need to write the function to do sampling. If that's the case, just write the 'd' function and then use the distribution in your model code. It should just work. 

If the algorithm you'll use does need the 'r' function, you can use any of the functionality documented for writing nimbleFunctions in your 'r' function, including looping and qnorm().  Others may have examples they can share. 

Chris

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Creating a User Defined Distribution: sampling
parts:
Hi Matt,

I was about to reply as well, so let me add to Chris' reply.  It's true that nimble allows you to write new distributions and also to write new samplers, but these are separate features.  Your email makes it sound like you might be under the impression that you can only add a distribution if you also have the wherewithal to provide a sampler, but that is not the case.  If you can provide the "d" function for your distribution, you can typically let nimble's built-in samplers take it from there.  For a univariate continuous distribution, the default sampler will be an adaptive random-walk Metropolis-Hastings sampler. 

I hope that helps.  Let us know further questions.

-Perry
